content: 1. Edoxaban and potent P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inducers (e.g., elivaldogene autotemcel, tenofovir DF): These drugs may reduce each other's effectiveness. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Patients should discontinue antiretroviral medications for at least one month before starting stem cell mobilization therapies and continue avoiding them until all apheresis cycles are completed. 2. Elivaldogene autotemcel and lamivudine: These drugs may reduce each other's effectiveness. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Antiretroviral medications should be discontinued at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapies and avoided until all apheresis cycles are completed. 3. Elivaldogene autotemcel and doravirine: These drugs may reduce each other's effectiveness. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Discontinue antiretroviral medications at least one month before starting stem cell mobilization therapies and avoid them until all apheresis cycles are completed. 4. Enasidenib and tenofovir DF: Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Avoid combining enasidenib with sensitive substrates of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP, as even minimal concentration changes may lead to severe toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 5. Fexinidazole and doravirine: Fexinidazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects for CYP3A4 substrates. 6. Doravirine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel: These drugs may interact. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Discontinue antiretroviral medications at least one month before starting stem cell mobilization therapies and avoid them until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period for complete elimination. 7. Lamivudine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel: These drugs may interact. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Discontinue antiretroviral medications at least one month before starting stem cell mobilization therapies and avoid them until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period for complete elimination. Antiretrovirals may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. 8. Lasmiditan and tenofovir DF: Lasmiditan increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Lasmiditan inhibits BCRP in vitro. Avoid co-administration with BCRP substrates. 9. Tucatinib and doravirine: Tucatinib increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Comment: Avoid combining tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 10. Abacavir and lamivudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 11. Abacavir and tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 12. Acalabrutinib and tenofovir DF: Acalabrutinib increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use with caution and monitor closely. Comment: Acalabrutinib may increase exposure to co-administered BCRP substrates. 13. Atazanavir and doravirine: Atazanavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 14. Atazanavir and lamivudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 15. Acyclovir and tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Acyclovir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use with caution and monitor closely. Comment: Co-administration of tenofovir with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum tenofovir concentrations. 16. Belzutifan and doravirine: Belzutifan decreases doravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Comment: If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates as per prescribing information. 17. Aldesleukin and tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Aldesleukin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 18. Amikacin and tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Amikacin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use with caution and monitor closely. 19. Tenofovir DF and amiloride: Tenofovir DF increases amiloride levels by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. There is potential for increased toxicity. 20. Amphotericin B (all formulations) and tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration may also increase tenofovir levels. Use with caution and monitor closely. 21. Apalutamide and tenofovir DF: Apalutamide decreases tenofovir DF levels by increasing elimination. Use with caution and monitor closely. Comment: Apalutamide weakly induces BCRP and may decrease systemic exposure of BCRP substrates. 22. Atazanavir and tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels by an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to loss of antiviral activity. Ritonavir boosting may help compensate. Use with caution and monitor closely. 23. Berotralstat and tenofovir DF: Berotralstat increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. Comment: Monitor or adjust the dose of P-gp substrates if co-administered. 24. Bleomycin and tenofovir DF: Bleomycin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. There is potential for increased toxicity. 25. Lamivudine and cabozantinib: Lamivudine increases cabozantinib levels. Use with caution and monitor closely. Comment: MRP2 inhibitors increase cabozantinib toxicity.
